source_caption:
Halle Berry initially struggled with Storm’s accent in X-Men, experimenting with different styles before ultimately dropping it in later films. The change helped her focus more on the character’s presence and authority rather than maintaining a forced voice.

X-Men (2000), directed by Bryan Singer, starring Hugh Jackman, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen. A groundbreaking superhero film that introduced the X-Men to the big screen, blending action and social themes about identity, acceptance, and belonging.

source_details.title: X-Men
source_details.synopsis: X-Men is a 2000 American superhero film based on the superhero team from Marvel Comics created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Bryan Singer from a screenplay by David Hayter and a story by Singer and Tom DeSanto, it features an ensemble cast consisting of Patrick Stewart, Hugh Jackman, Ian McKellen, Halle Berry, Famke Janssen, James Marsden, Bruce Davison, Rebecca Romijn, Ray Park, and Anna Paquin. The film depicts a world where an unknown proportion of people are mutants, possessing superhuman powers that make them distrusted by normal humans.
